section_summary: This section begins with Japanese consular registration cards, apparently for residents of Cuba, and then turns to Allied efforts to secure, examine, and dispose of former Japanese diplomatic archives, funds, buildings, and other property around the world. A long SCAP compilation reproduces Japanese Foreign Ministry telegrams implementing the October 1945 surrender directive in Sweden, Switzerland, Portugal, Afghanistan, Ireland, the Vatican, and associated consular posts. The final pages concern policy disagreements over preservation or sale of Japanese property and include the opening portion of a translated 1942 diary by former Japanese Minister to Chile Yamagata, describing intelligence work, Axis diplomatic coordination, and efforts to prevent the expulsion of a Mitsui manager.

subfiles.title: Japanese consular registration cards for residents in Cuba
subfiles.about: Registration cards record personal details, family relationships, addresses, occupations, passports, and arrivals of Japanese residents in Cuba.
subfiles.summary: The surviving cards concern people including members of the Ichihara, Uchiyama, Inakura, Ishizaki, and Ishikawa families. They give Japanese domiciles, Cuban addresses, arrival dates, passport numbers, occupations, and family members, although the OCR is especially poor and page 232 is blank.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 6784: Examination of Archives of Former Japanese Legation in Stockholm
subfiles.from: C. M. Ravndal, American Legation, Stockholm
subfiles.about: Reports the examination and custody of the former Japanese Legation archives in Stockholm.
subfiles.summary: Ravndal reports that Commander Rufus L. Taylor examined the archives and found no documents of major intelligence value. Duplicate documents of possible interest were removed with four-power consent, while a report that the Japanese code machine had been broken up and thrown into a canal remained unconfirmed.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on examination of the former Japanese Legation archives
subfiles.about: Summarizes Taylor's findings and recommendations after examining the Japanese archives in Stockholm.
subfiles.summary: Taylor found little documentary intelligence because Japanese officials had ample time to destroy sensitive material. He recommends ending further Navy exploitation of the files while preparing tightly controlled interrogations of Japanese personnel, especially General Onodera and Admiral Abe.

subfiles.title: Enclosure A: Log of activities during the Stockholm archives examination
subfiles.about: Chronicles Taylor's travel, archival examination, consultations, and proposed interrogation program from January 3 through 12, 1946.
subfiles.summary: Taylor traveled through Bremen and Copenhagen to Stockholm, inspected the Japanese chancery, safes, baggage, code room, and surviving files, and found evidence of extensive shredding and burning. Discussions with diplomatic, military, naval, and OSS officers shifted attention toward interrogating Japanese personnel before their possible departure from Europe.

subfiles.title: Enclosure B: List of documents of possible interest
subfiles.about: Lists low-value records selected from the former Japanese Legation archives.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure B lists documents of possible interest: Foreign Ministry manuals, files on Swedish economic conditions, and four cipher despatches from Dublin to Stockholm.

subfiles.title: Enclosure C: Memorandum on exploitation of the former Japanese Legation archives
subfiles.about: Recommends a coordinated program for exploiting the archives and interrogating senior Japanese personnel in Sweden.
subfiles.summary: Taylor describes the four-power committee controlling the archives and identifies Admiral Abe and General Onodera as potentially valuable interrogation targets. He urges State, War, Navy, and the Stockholm Legation to prepare coordinated programs rather than undertake hasty questioning.

subfiles.title: Airgram No. 1396 concerning German and Japanese archives in Addis Ababa
subfiles.about: Suggests using the Department's Japanese-archives instructions as a procedural model for German archives.
subfiles.summary: Airgram 1396: handle German archives under earlier instructions where practicable, report preliminary findings, and use Circular Airgram 3610 for Japanese archives in Addis Ababa.

subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-130 on Japanese archives in Brussels
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests local examination and preservation of selected Japanese archival materials pending arrival of experts.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-130: State can't yet send Japanese-language experts; Brussels should transcribe indexes of pro- and anti-Japanese persons and personnel lists, study films more closely, and preserve the archives.

subfiles.title: Instruction on custody of Japanese government property in Venezuela
subfiles.about: Seeks clarification of who controls Japanese government accounts and explains Allied trusteeship policy.
subfiles.summary: Instruction asks whether the Four Powers or Venezuela hold the Japanese government account; if Allied-held, tell Venezuela it's in trusteeship pending decisions considering Venezuelan claims and the Mexico City resolutions.

subfiles.title: Japanese Official Funds in the American Republics
subfiles.about: Reviews wartime policy toward Japanese official funds and proposes leaving locally blocked funds with American governments.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Japanese official funds in the American republics: after the effort to block Axis funds and SCAP's transfer order, it proposes not demanding transfer since sums are small, attaching draft instructions for Quito, Caracas, Bogota and San Salvador.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 36 on Japanese property in the Vatican
subfiles.from: Harold H. Tittmann Jr., Vatican City
subfiles.about: Reports discussions with Montini over disposal of Japanese property and assets in the Vatican.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 36: Tittmann is discussing disposal of Japanese property and assets in the Vatican with Montini per the February instruction, and will report.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 699: Japanese Records and Archives in Turkey
subfiles.from: Herbert S. Bursley, American Embassy, Ankara
subfiles.about: Reports the takeover and preliminary review of Japanese records in Turkey.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 699: the American, British, Chinese and Soviet embassies took over Japanese papers in Turkey February 15 and sealed them in the American Embassy; Chinese readers found nothing valuable, so Bursley advises against sending an examination team.

subfiles.title: List of Japanese papers taken over in Ankara
subfiles.about: Inventories the routine Japanese diplomatic papers placed in Allied custody in Ankara.
subfiles.summary: List of Japanese papers taken over in Ankara, 1941-1945: foreign ministry and mission correspondence, accounts and miscellany, largest category twelve account dossiers.

subfiles.title: Airgram instructing Beirut to preserve Japanese archives
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Orders that no action be taken on Japanese archives until the Department resolves issues raised by British instructions.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: Beirut's request for guidance is under study given British Foreign Office instructions; take no action pending further directions.

subfiles.title: Beirut telegram concerning disposition of Japanese property
subfiles.about: Seeks guidance on proposals for disposing of Japanese property in Beirut.
subfiles.summary: The heavily damaged text appears to discuss British, American, and Soviet views on selling Japanese furniture or other effects and disposing of emblems and related items. It asks the Department for instructions before a common Allied decision is implemented.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 344 forwarding SCAP communications on Japanese diplomatic property
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP's compilation of communications implementing the October 25, 1945 archives-and-property directive.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 344 transmits SCAP's March 30 letter and enclosures on Japanese Foreign Ministry instructions to former missions on transferring diplomatic records and property.

subfiles.title: SCAP letter listing communications on transfer of diplomatic and consular property
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Lists twenty-nine Japanese telegrams concerning surrender of diplomatic and consular property and archives.
subfiles.summary: The letter enumerates communications sent to or received from Japanese representatives in Sweden, Switzerland, Portugal, Afghanistan, Dublin, the Vatican, Zurich, and other posts. It notes which items had been transmitted previously and that two full sets were supplied to the Political Adviser in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 840 on initial Allied demands
subfiles.to: Japanese ministers in Sweden, Switzerland, Portugal, and Afghanistan, and consul general in Dublin
subfiles.about: Reports Allied demands concerning protecting powers, property, archives, and the recall of Japanese diplomats.
subfiles.summary: Translated telegram 840: Allied demands that Sweden and Switzerland act as protecting powers, Japanese missions surrender property and archives, and neutral-state representatives return home; Tokyo questions their legal basis under the Potsdam Declaration.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 851 ordering surrender of Japanese diplomatic property
subfiles.to: Japanese ministers in Sweden and Switzerland
subfiles.about: Orders compliance with the Allied directive and transfer of Japanese property and archives.
subfiles.summary: Translated telegram 851 orders ministers to secure transfer of Japanese property in Allied countries, surrender their missions' property and archives, cease official dealings, arrange protection, report and prepare to return.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 852 to Portugal, Afghanistan, and Dublin
subfiles.to: Japanese ministers in Portugal and Afghanistan and consul general in Dublin
subfiles.about: Orders surrender of diplomatic and consular property and suspension of official relations.
subfiles.summary: Translated telegram 852 to Portugal, Afghanistan and Dublin: transfer property and archives intact to Allied representatives, report completion, and recall staff while a protecting power is pending.

subfiles.title: Stockholm report on sealing of Japanese offices
subfiles.about: Reports the sealing of Japanese diplomatic, military, and naval offices in Stockholm.
subfiles.summary: Stockholm: after the minister told Sweden's foreign minister of Tokyo's instructions, British, American and Soviet representatives sealed the legation and attaché offices.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1047 from Bern
subfiles.about: Reports notification of the Swiss government regarding the surrender instructions.
subfiles.summary: Bern telegram 1047: the minister told the Swiss foreign minister of Telegram 851 on November 1; no completed transfer yet.

subfiles.title: Telegram Tokyo No. 2 from Afghanistan
subfiles.about: Reports inventories, Allied inspection, and provisional arrangements for the closed Japanese Legation in Afghanistan.
subfiles.summary: Afghanistan: after Allied demands for inventories, American, French and Chinese officials inspected; immediate removal being impracticable, Japanese staff may stay temporarily but will lower the flag and end official relations.

subfiles.title: Dublin report on preliminary transfer arrangements
subfiles.about: Reports preliminary negotiations over transfer of the Dublin consulate and repatriation of its staff.
subfiles.summary: Badly damaged Dublin telegram on contacts with Allied representatives about transferring property and archives, closing the office, repatriation and protecting Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 459 clarifying the Swiss transfer
subfiles.about: Clarifies that official funds are included and that sealing alone does not constitute transfer.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 459: the minister must physically hand property and archives to Allied representatives, report housing problems from surrendering residences, and Switzerland's protecting-power actions and the Zurich consulate.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 876 clarifying transfers in Portugal, Afghanistan, and Dublin
subfiles.to: Japanese ministers in Portugal and Afghanistan and consul general in Dublin
subfiles.about: Clarifies that government funds must be transferred and sealing is insufficient.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 876: Portugal, Afghanistan and Dublin must complete actual transfer of official property and archives and report housing problems; Portugal's minister also reports on the Macau consulate.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 269 to Sweden
subfiles.about: Orders actual transfer of government funds, property, and archives in Sweden.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 269 to Sweden: governmental funds are included but private property isn't, sealing alone is inadequate, and Sweden should report measures taken as protecting power.

subfiles.title: Special Telegram No. 3 from Afghanistan
subfiles.about: Explains why formal surrender of the legation was postponed until the minister's departure.
subfiles.summary: Afghanistan special telegram 3: immediate removal was impossible for lack of accommodation and furniture, and the American chargé accepted postponing formal transfer.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 46 ordering immediate compliance in Dublin
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's urgent order for the consul general to obey Allied representatives.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 46 orders Dublin's consul general to report personally to the American Consulate, hand over documents, property and keys, and notify the American and British missions.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1053 on delays in Switzerland
subfiles.about: Explains legal and diplomatic obstacles delaying transfer of Japanese property in Switzerland.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1053: Switzerland inventories were ready but Swiss authorization was needed for buildings and frozen deposits; Bern sought U.S. clarification on protecting Japanese interests, so transfer wasn't complete.

subfiles.title: Lisbon report on property and Yokohama Specie Bank funds
subfiles.about: Reports negotiations over funds, property, and the Macau consulate.
subfiles.summary: Lisbon: the Allies rejected the claim that Yokohama Specie Bank funds at the legation were private; other funds were being transferred, but technical and logistical issues delayed completion in Lisbon and Macau.

subfiles.title: Telegram Toku No. 7 from Dublin
subfiles.about: Objects that Allied demands in Dublin extend beyond Tokyo's instructions.
subfiles.summary: The American consul general and British commercial secretary demanded extensive information on private property, Japanese residents, consular employees, and third-country belongings. The Japanese consul insisted he was ready to transfer government property, archives, and keys but sought clarification and information about repatriation expenses.

subfiles.title: Telegram Common No. 905 restricting communications
subfiles.to: Japanese representatives in Switzerland, Portugal, Afghanistan, and Ireland
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's prohibition on communications unrelated to the property-transfer directive.
subfiles.summary: Telegram Common 905 orders representatives to stop communicating with Tokyo except as needed for the October 25 archives and property directive, reflecting tighter SCAP supervision.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 276 restricting communications with Sweden
subfiles.about: Applies SCAP's communications prohibition to the former Japanese mission in Sweden.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 276 orders Sweden's post to end all communications except those implementing the October 25 directive, like other neutral-country posts.

subfiles.title: Swedish legation report on completed surrender and repatriation
subfiles.about: Reports completion of the Stockholm inventory and requests help repatriating Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: Swedish legation report: chancery and attaché offices sealed, funds surrendered, full inventory certified; staff health, Sweden's protection work, and no shipping for about seventy Japanese nationals.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 50 to Consul-General Beppu
subfiles.about: Orders Beppu to deliver the inventory and comply with expanded Allied demands.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 50 to Consul-General Beppu: Yoshida says the demands aim to separate official from private property, not seize belongings, and warns delay may prompt unilateral Allied action.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 51 listing information demanded in Ireland
subfiles.about: Enumerates records, keys, and property information to be delivered to Allied representatives.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 51 lists information demanded in Ireland: leases, solicitors, employees, residents, inventories, car records, bankbooks, keys, property locations and English copies of instructions.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 52 urging immediate Dublin compliance
subfiles.about: Repeats the order to meet Allied requirements without delay.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 52, citing Telegram 50, commands immediate compliance with Allied representatives in Dublin, fearing forcible action.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1054 on Swiss protection and property transfer
subfiles.about: Reports Switzerland's refusal to protect Japanese interests under American conditions and plans to transfer property.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1054: Switzerland declined Japan's broader protecting-power request after talks with the U.S.; Japanese property and archives, including Zurich and Geneva consulates', pass to Switzerland and then to Allied representatives.

subfiles.title: Urgent Telegram No. 46 to the Japanese mission at the Vatican
subfiles.about: Orders surrender of mission property and archives, termination of official relations, and repatriation.
subfiles.summary: Urgent telegram 46 to the Vatican mission: transfer all property, funds and archives to Allied representatives, end Vatican relations, send staff home, list repatriates, and limit communications to SCAP-authorized matters.

subfiles.title: Lisbon report on transfer of the Macau consulate
subfiles.about: Reports completion of the Japanese consulate-property transfer in Macau.
subfiles.summary: Lisbon: the Macau consulate gave custody to Chinese representatives on December 8; staff may use furniture until departure, with Chinese arranging transport from Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Zurich report on transfer of consular funds and property
subfiles.about: Reports surrender of Zurich consular funds, archives, and property to Swiss authorities.
subfiles.summary: Zurich: Swiss federal officials took the consulate's property and funds, over sixty thousand francs, sealed the office, and received an inventory of the official residence.

subfiles.title: Geneva report on transfer of consular funds and property
subfiles.about: Reports the Swiss inventory and sealing of the Japanese consulate in Geneva.
subfiles.summary: Geneva: cantonal officials inventoried the consulate before Consul Yoshioka and sealed two rooms; 10,516.67 francs were handed over, with residential property to follow.

subfiles.title: Bern report on transfer of legation property and funds
subfiles.about: Details the transfer of the Bern legation, archives, and large cash and bank balances to Swiss authorities.
subfiles.summary: Swiss officials sealed the chancery and archive cabinets, inventoried the residence, and accepted cash and accounts associated with the legation, attachés, other European posts, and Yokohama Specie Bank. The protocol reserved money for repatriation and closing expenses and acknowledged uncertainty about privately owned sums within diplomatic accounts.

subfiles.title: Vatican Telegram No. 90
subfiles.about: Reports readiness to transfer mission property and archives through the Vatican.
subfiles.summary: Vatican telegram 90: the Japanese envoy notified the Vatican December 20 that his mission is ready to surrender its property and archives and asked it to tell Allied representatives; no response yet.

subfiles.title: Vatican Telegram No. 91
subfiles.about: Reports completed transfer of archives and termination of official Vatican relations.
subfiles.summary: Vatican telegram 91: the envoy says the archives were transferred through the Vatican on December 31 per Allied directions, and the mission formally ended its official Vatican connection.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Despatch No. 344 forwarding SCAP communications
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the covering despatch forwarding SCAP's communications on Japanese diplomatic property.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Despatch 344's cover page, identifying SCAP's March 30 compilation of Foreign Ministry communications implementing the October 25, 1945 directive.

subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-141 on Japanese archives in Lima
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests a locally arranged preliminary examination of Japanese archives pending assignment of specialists.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-141: with no Japanese-language experts available, Lima should arrange a preliminary inspection with other Allied representatives, keeping the archives available for fuller examination.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 863 transmitting Siamese receipts
subfiles.about: Transmits receipts for advances made to the Siamese Legation by the former Japanese minister in Lisbon.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 863 sends two receipts signed by Colonel Mom Snidvongsseni for advances by the former Japanese minister on April 5 and July 19, 1945.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 261 on Japanese property in Finland
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet expectations concerning division of Japanese property in Finland.
subfiles.summary: Helsinki telegram 261: British and Soviet legations learned the Department's policy, but a Soviet official expects the property divided among the four powers, not in a joint trust account; Hamilton will follow Washington's instructions.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3364 on Japanese archives in Rome
subfiles.about: Forwards an exchange of notes with the Soviet Embassy about Japanese property and archives in Italy.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 3364 sends three documents recording American and Soviet discussions in Rome on four-power control, property disposal and examining and copying the archives.

subfiles.title: American memorandum to the Soviet Embassy on Japanese property in Italy
subfiles.about: Sets out the United States position on custody, disposal, and examination of Japanese property and archives in Italy.
subfiles.summary: American memorandum to the Soviet Embassy supports joint four-power control of Japanese property in Italy under local procedures, favors selling official property but protecting private belongings, offers American examiners and asks about Soviet specialists.

subfiles.title: Soviet Note Verbale on examination of Japanese archives
subfiles.from: Embassy of the Soviet Union, Rome
subfiles.to: Embassy of the United States, Rome
subfiles.about: Accepts Chinese participation and proposes joint selection and copying of important Japanese documents.
subfiles.summary: Soviet note: no Japanese-language specialist is available, no objection to including China, and it proposes American, Chinese and British experts select documents with a Soviet representative present, with copies for all four powers.

subfiles.title: American Note Verbale on the Rome archives examination
subfiles.from: Embassy of the United States, Rome
subfiles.to: Embassy of the Soviet Union, Rome
subfiles.about: Explains how the American team will examine and classify the former Japanese Embassy archives.
subfiles.summary: American note: after Allied military authorities finish the villa inventory, American investigators will classify the Rome archives and share findings; the four representatives choose material to photograph, and the Soviet may observe.

subfiles.title: Canberra airgram on Japanese diplomatic records in Australia
subfiles.about: Reports the start of the Commonwealth government's examination of Japanese diplomatic property.
subfiles.summary: Canberra: Australian authorities had just begun examining Japanese records and thought them of little value; the Legation will get a description and Washington can decide on sending a team.

subfiles.title: Birch memorandum on revising the MacArthur property directive
subfiles.about: Supports an SPD proposal to amend the directive governing Japanese official property abroad.
subfiles.summary: Birch sees no Eastern Hemisphere objection to modifying MacArthur's joint-custody directive and asks concurrence before clearing it with Surrey and other offices.

subfiles.title: Proposed Revision of MacArthur Directive on Japanese Official Property
subfiles.about: Compares British and American property policy and recommends loosening mandatory custody requirements.
subfiles.summary: Memo contrasts American preservation with British willingness to destroy examined archives and sell movables; to ease friction, SPD proposes amending the directive so flags and propaganda may be destroyed and official or perishable private property sold, archives kept as public records, proceeds in trust.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 13,881 transmitting Part III of Yamagata's diary
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers, American Embassy, Santiago
subfiles.about: Forwards the third installment of a translation of former Japanese Minister Yamagata's diary.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 13,881 sends Part III of Yamagata's diary, found in a chest at the Swedish Legation, covering August 1 to October 31, 1942; copy to the British Embassy.

subfiles.title: Some Facts in Former Japanese Minister Yamagata's Diary, Part III
subfiles.from: Yamagata, former Japanese Minister to Chile
subfiles.about: Records intelligence work, Axis diplomatic contacts, Chilean politics, and efforts to protect Mitsui manager Miyasaki during August and early September 1942.
subfiles.summary: Yamagata's diary, Part III: intelligence cables, meetings with Chilean and Axis diplomats, fear President Rios might break with the Axis, appeals to stop Mitsui manager Miyasaki's arrest and expulsion, propaganda contacts, Brazil's war declaration and the planned Ministry of Great Eastern Asia.
